title: model catalog release sync: publish script deletes stale JSON assets after upload
answers: Why does a deleted model catalog JSON file still download from the model-catalog/latest release?
How do I remove an old catalog asset from the GitHub release?
Does publishing the model catalog touch non-JSON release assets?
body:
Path: `dev/publish_model_catalog.sh` (run by the `publish` job) creates the `model-catalog/latest` release if missing, uploads every `*.json` file from `--catalog-dir` with `--clobber`, and then runs the stale-asset cleanup loop after `gh release upload`.
Rule: The release's JSON assets mirror the catalog directory. After a successful upload, each release asset whose name ends in `.json` and has no matching file in `CATALOG_DIR` is deleted with `gh release delete-asset`. Deletion happens only after upload succeeds, so a failed upload cannot remove valid assets.
Symptom: After a catalog JSON file was removed on master, its old release asset stayed downloadable from the model-catalog/latest release.
Constraints: Only names ending in `.json` are considered; other release assets are left alone. The cleanup relies on `set -euo pipefail`, so an upload failure stops the script before deletion. Applies only to the release tag passed via `--tag`.
applies: Model catalog release publication script; changes to how catalog assets are synced to GitHub releases.
says: Deleted model catalog files are still available for download from the latest release.
Removed catalog definitions should be cleaned up from the published release assets.
Old catalog entries continue to download even after being deleted from the repository.
Ensure obsolete catalog items are removed when publishing an updated release.
The release download list still contains deprecated model catalog items after updates.
search: dev/publish_model_catalog.sh syncs release assets to mirror the catalog directory by deleting stale JSON assets using gh release delete-asset after upload. Deletion runs only after a successful gh release upload and only targets assets ending in .json that lack a matching file in CATALOG_DIR. Non-JSON release assets are left alone, and an upload failure aborts the script before any deletion occurs.
